item.title: python3Packages.raven: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA file
item.description:
Part of #576541 and #576542.

raven has a bundled CA file, raven/data/cacert.pem. raven uses this file for HTTPS connections when it cannot import certifi. This change replaces the file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert in postPatch. Thus, the installed package and the wheel in the dist output get the cacert bundle.

[!WARNING] AI Disclosure: Claude Code made the code change, the commit message and the first version of this pull request description. Claude Code used Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. I examined all of this work. Claude Code also wrote all of nix-cacert-harness. In the second part of the output, the harness adds a temporary test root to cacert and builds the package again. Then raven sends a request to a local openssl s_server from a Python environment without certifi. The certificate of this server chains to the test root. Before this change, cacert has no effect on the result. After this change, it has an effect. To examine the server certificate, raven uses ssl.wrap_socket, but Python 3.12 removed this function. Thus, with Python 3.12 and higher, HTTPS requests from raven stop before TLS starts, with or without this change. The test adds an equivalent function to examine the trust store. This problem is in raven upstream and is not related to this change.

item.title: rubyPackages.{algoliasearch,excon,httpclient,nap}: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA files
item.description:
Part of #576541.

The gems excon, httpclient, nap and algoliasearch each have a bundled CA file. httpclient, nap and algoliasearch use their file as the trust store. excon adds its file to the trust store. This change adds postInstall entries in pkgs/development/ruby-modules/gem-config/default.nix. These entries replace each file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert. Each entry replaces a file only if the file is there. Thus, other versions of the gems continue to build. httpclient also has a file that it does not use, cacert1024.pem. This change replaces that file too.

item.title: temurin-bin: generate cacerts from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

Heads up, most of this change is a reindent – you can press "hide whitespace" in the diff to make it easier to read.

The Temurin binary JDKs, temurin-bin and temurin-jre-bin, have a bundled Java trust store, lib/security/cacerts. This change makes a new cacerts from the cacert bundle with jre-generate-cacerts, as the merged openjdk change #576518 does. temurin-bin is also the bootstrap JDK of openjdk. Thus, this change adds the argument regenerateCacerts, and openjdk sets it to false for its bootstrap JDK. The drvPath of each openjdk does not change. This change does not change jmods/java.base.jmod or the darwin packages.

The JDKs semeru-bin and semeru-jre-bin also come from temurin-bin/jdk-linux-base.nix. At this time, their JVM does not start on nixpkgs, and it shows this error: cannot enable executable stack as shared object requires: Invalid argument. This occurs because glibc 2.41 and newer versions do not accept a library that must have an executable stack, and libj9vm29.so is such a library. Thus, it is not possible to use keytool at build time. This change sets regenerateCacerts = false for these two packages, and their drvPath does not change. The repair of these two packages (a new version, or meta.broken) is a different task.

item.title: caddy: use only the system CA store
item.description:
Caddy imports golang.org/x/crypto/x509roots/fallback in cmd/x509rootsfallback.go. That bundle contains the eMudhra emSign roots, including emSign ECC Root CA - G3. Go uses it when no system roots load, for example in a container without /etc/ssl. It does not get cacert updates.

Tested on x86_64-linux, plain and with a plugin (replace-response):

Note: the hash in plugins.test.nix is already out of date on master before this change; it is not touched here.

item.title: cpython: make bundled pip prefer the system CA bundle
item.description:
pip vendors certifi and adds its cacert.pem to the trust store next to the system store. Every venv made with python -m venv gets this pip from ensurepip. Thus a cacert update alone does not remove a distrusted root (for example emSign ECC Root CA - G3) from pip in a venv.

Rewrite the bundled pip wheel so that its vendored certifi returns NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_FILE or /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt when one exists. The vendored bundle stays as a fallback.

The override lives in pkgs/development/interpreters/python/pip-certifi-override.py. The python3Packages.pip PR appends the same file to its own vendored certifi: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/576525

Tested on x86_64-linux with python3 3.14 (same diff on master): in a venv, pip download six with SSL_CERT_FILE set to an unrelated self-signed cert fails, and with the system bundle it works. Before the change both worked, because pip also trusted its vendored bundle.

Related to: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/576485 Related to: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/576542

item.title: openjdk: generate cacerts from cacert for JDK 11+
item.description:
JDK 8 already builds its cacerts from cacert. JDK 11 and later shipped the CA list that comes with the OpenJDK source. That list does not get the cacert updates, for example the removal of distrusted roots.

Generate the keystore with the bootstrap keytool before configure and give it to --with-cacerts-file. The file goes into the java.base jmod, so jlink images such as jre_minimal also use it.

Write a PKCS12 store without a password, like upstream. The JDK opens cacerts without a password, so it cannot read certificates that a password protects.

Closes: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/210241 Related to: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/576485 Related to: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/576543

This reverses 5a53b98248d7 ("openjdk10: Use included cacerts", 2018). That commit gave no reason. Since then the bundled list has gone stale between JDK releases, and the eMudhra distrust shows the cost: the JDK 11+ store still holds emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services.

Tested on x86_64-linux with openjdk21_headless (same diff on master):

  • keytool -list -cacerts opens without a password: PKCS12, 118 entries. Their SHA-256 fingerprints match the 118 server-auth roots of cacert 3.131.1. AAA (email trust only in cacert) and emSign ECC Root CA - G3 are gone.
  • A jlink minimal JRE gets a byte-identical lib/security/cacerts.
  • HTTPS to github.com works with the default store; with JAVAX_NET_SSL_TRUSTSTORE set to a store without the needed root it fails with "PKIX path building failed".
  • openjdk11, openjdk17_headless, openjdk21, openjdk25 and jre_minimal instantiate on staging.

Note: the cacerts format cannot carry the NSS "distrust after" dates, so those are lost, as they already are for JDK 8.

item.title: nushell: eMudhra fixes
item.description:
Two fixes for the eMudhra intermediate compromise:

  • version check used update-informer's default ureq agent, which trusts only the compiled-in webpki-roots. Patch it to use nushell's own TLS config (tls_config), so it uses the system CA store like http get already does.
  • Bump webpki-roots to 1.0.10 (drops emSign ECC Root CA - G3) and rustls-webpki to 0.103.16 (blocks the eight revoked eMudhra intermediate SPKIs) through a Cargo.lock patch.

Both changes are already merged upstream, after the 0.116.1 release: https://github.com/nushell/nushell/pull/19298 (version check uses nushell's own HTTP client and TLS config) and https://github.com/nushell/nushell/pull/19308 (webpki-roots 1.0.10, webpki-root-certs 1.0.10, rustls-webpki 0.103.16). Drop both patches when nushell is updated to a release that contains them.

Tested on x86_64-linux: build with the full cargo test check phase, http get and version check with SSL_CERT_FILE set to an unrelated root fail, and with the system bundle they work.

Related to: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/576485 Related to: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/576544
